Most local-service visitors arrive on a phone. Starting from the narrow layout makes you choose what matters.
Write base styles for small screens and add min-width queries as content needs.
Design only for a desktop mockup.
A breakpoint belongs where the layout breaks, not at a device width. Resize the window and add one where lines get too long.
Set breakpoints where content needs them, in rem.
Without a viewport tag, phones render a desktop-width page scaled down and the layout never responds.
Include width=device-width, initial-scale=1 in the head.
Sideways scrolling on a phone is a sign of a fixed-width element. Find the offender and fix it.
Check at 320px; use max-width:100% on media and wrap tables in a scroll region.
Hide it with overflow-x:hidden on body.
Smaller text forces zooming on phones and iOS zooms into inputs below 16px.
Set the base size to 1rem or larger and inputs to 16px.
Wide tables break narrow screens. Allow the table's region to scroll, labelled and focusable.
Wrap in a region with overflow-x:auto, tabindex='0' and a label.
A card in a sidebar and in a main column needs different layouts at the same viewport width. Container queries style by the container.
Fake it with viewport media queries.
A dropdown that opens on hover can not be opened on touch. Use click or focus-within as well.
Open menus on click or focus; hover is an extra.
A wide landscape crop becomes a speck on a phone. picture lets you serve a tighter crop.
Use picture with media sources, and object-position to keep the subject.
Cramped lines tire the eye and fail the text-spacing test. Body text reads best near 1.5.
Set unitless line-height 1.5 for body, 1.1 to 1.25 for large headings.
Use one tight line-height for all text.
Short lines break rhythm; long lines make people lose their place.
Use max-width in ch units on paragraph containers.
A modular scale of five or six sizes creates hierarchy. Many in-between sizes flatten it.
Define sizes as tokens, with clear steps between heading levels.
Pick sizes ad hoc until headings and body are similar.
Hierarchy comes from contrast in size, weight and colour. Text at nearly the same size reads flat.
Make each level distinct, with at least a 1.25 ratio.
Use one family at one weight for everything.
text-wrap:balance evens line lengths so headings avoid a single orphan word on the last line.
Apply text-wrap:balance to headings and pretty to paragraphs.
Proportional digits make columns of prices wobble. tabular-nums aligns them.
Leave digits proportional in price tables.
A fallback with different proportions makes text jump when the web font arrives. size-adjust and ascent overrides limit the shift.
Switch from Arial to a very different face.
All caps slows reading and screen readers may spell abbreviations. Reserve it for short labels, and our lint avoids small uppercase labels above every heading.
Write in sentence case; use capitals for one-word tags at most.
Set paragraphs or subtitles in uppercase.
Justified text without hyphenation leaves rivers of white space, hard for dyslexic readers.
Left-align body text; justify only with hyphens:auto in wide columns.
Monospace Is for Code and Data
A monospace body face reads as costume and is slow for paragraphs. Use it for code, numbers and tables.
Set code and tabular data in monospace; text in a text face.
Truncate With Access to the Full Text
Ellipses hide names, addresses and prices. If the cut hides something needed, provide it in full elsewhere.
Truncate decoration only; wrap essential text, or reveal it on expand.
Cut a price or address with an ellipsis.
04/05/26 means different days to different readers. Spell out the month and use the user's locale.
Format with Intl.DateTimeFormat and include the month name.
1234567 is hard to read and a price without a currency is ambiguous. Intl.NumberFormat handles grouping and symbols.
Format with Intl.NumberFormat and the right currency code.
Lorem ipsum, 'Your title here' and stock names reach live pages more often than anyone admits. Real content shapes the design.
Write real copy first; fail the build on known placeholders.
Short sentences and common words help everyone, and are essential for readers with cognitive or language difficulties.
Aim for a lower secondary reading level and define jargon.
Fill pages with buzzwords such as seamless or elevate.
We fix boilers the same day.
'Submit' and 'Get started' tell people little. A verb plus object states the result.
Label with verb and object: Book a visit, Get a quote.
Made-up testimonials, ratings and statistics destroy trust and may break advertising law. Every figure comes from the owner and can be checked.
Use real, named quotes and numbers with a source; drop the row if none exist.
Stock photos of people at laptops tell visitors nothing. Photos of the real team, work and premises build recognition.
Use photos of the actual business with meaningful alt text.
